decision.explanation: Since w=u+v, linearity gives Aw=Au+Av=u′+v′=[7e^{7t}, 2e^{2t}]ᵀ. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7t} \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=u(t)+v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}({e}^{7t})^{′} \\ ({e}^{2t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7{e}^{7t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since u(t) and v(t) are solutions to x′(t)=Ax(t), the superposition principle guarantees that cu(t)+dv(t) is also a solution to x′(t)=Ax(t) for all c,d∈R.

Notice that w(t)=u(t)+v(t).

Therefore, w is a solution to x′(t)=Ax(t). So, in order to find Aw(t) we just need to find w′(t) as follows: Aw=w′(t)=[(e7t)′(e2t)′]=[7e7t2e2t].

Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=u(t)+v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}({e}^{7t})^{′} \\ ({e}^{2t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7{e}^{7t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}-5{e}^{2t} \\ 3{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=-5u(t)+3v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-5{e}^{2t})^{′} \\ (3{e}^{-3t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10{e}^{2t} \\ -9{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=-5u(t)+3v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$

$$

after.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}9{e}^{4t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=9u(t)+2v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(9{e}^{4t})^{′} \\ (2{e}^{2t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}36{e}^{4t} \\ 4{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
